jena: Quick mini-sweep results for Mistral-7B(instruct) vs Llama-2-7B(chat). A100 vs H100, three regions (us-west1 / eu-central1 / ap-southeast1).
jena: Test config: batch=1, prefill=512, decode=512, q4_0, 60s steady-state runs per cell. no KV cache warmups.
bench-bot: Uploading raw CSV + charts: https://dash.internal/runs/1747500000 (permissions: eng-ml) :rocket:
maria: Pasting condensed CSV for quick eyeballs:
```
model,hw,region,prefill_ms,decode_ms,tokens_per_sec,$_per_1M_tokens
mistral-7b,H100,us-west1,118,275,3620,0.92
mistral-7b,A100,us-west1,172,420,2420,1.36
llama2-7b,H100,us-west1,132,305,3330,1.05
llama2-7b,A100,us-west1,188,465,2190,1.48
mistral-7b,H100,eu-central1,130,305,3400,0.98
mistral-7b,A100,eu-central1,185,445,2300,1.44
mistral-7b,H100,ap-southeast1,145,335,3100,1.10
mistral-7b,A100,ap-southeast1,205,495,2000,1.68
```
kevin: Nice. Is tokens_per_sec measured end-to-end (including prefill) or decode-only?
maria: tokens_per_sec is steady-state decode throughput (decode path only). prefill_ms is one-off per-request cost. we measured end-to-end latency separately.
kevin: Got it. So $/1M is calculated from instance-cost and measured tokens/sec? numbers assume on-demand GPU pricing of our infra, right?
maria: Correct — derived from per-GPU cost bucket used in infra (includes amortized infra + energy), no reserved discounts. formula: (GPU_hour_cost / tokens_per_sec) * 3600 * 1e6^{-1} simplified to the table.
anya: Any quality regressions with q4_0? we care about hallucination / safety for L2-7b on instruction prompts.
maria: Ran eval-set (500 prompts, instruction-style). Mistral-7B q4_0: avg BLEU-like score delta -0.4% vs fp16, hallucination rate +0.6pp on a small prompt subset (edge-case factual QA). Llama2-7B q4_0: delta -0.9%, hallucination +1.1pp. flagged 23 prompts for human review.
jena: Observations: H100 gives ~1.5x decode throughput for 7B on q4_0 vs A100 in these runs. prefill latencies ~30-40% lower on H100. APAC region shows thermal/packing hit — ~15-20% worse than us-west for same SKU.
tom: Which kernel build? did we use nvfuser/fused or fallback? any long-context fallthroughs?
maria: H100 -> cuDNN-fused + nvfuser kernels enabled. A100 -> hand-tuned tiled kernels (older baseline). We saw kernel fallback on contexts >1024 tokens for certain attention variants on A100 (triggered nvlink fragmentation + runtime fallback) — explains some of the extra decode_ms on A100.
kevin: For production recommendation: H100 for latency-sensitive SLOs, A100 for committed reserved capacity if cost curve favors it? thoughts on $/1M tradeoffs?
jena: TL;DR: H100 wins for low-latency and better dollar-per-token at on-demand pricing in our runs (because throughput gains dominate price delta). However, for annual reserved A100 contracts, A100 can be cheaper per-token if you normalize discounts (we have customers where A100 committed capacity was 0.7x on-demand price -> flips economics).
anya: Any regressions when moving from q4_0 -> q8 (if available) or fp16?
maria: q8 (int8) improved decode throughput ~+20% but quality delta increased for both models (mistral ~-1.8% score). So q8 only for tolerant workloads. fp16 baseline still best quality with higher cost.
bench-bot: Aggregated chart refs: 1) decode_throughput_by_hw_region 2) prefill_latency_box 3) $per_1M_token_map. Links: https://dash.internal/runs/1747500000/charts (eng-ml access).
tom: Action items: 1) run a 10k prompt eval for the flagged hallucination prompts (maria) 2) sweep reserved pricing sensitivity for A100/H100 (finance + infra) 3) add a 2k-context kernel-stability test for A100 (eng-runtime).
maria: Will queue the eval + upload raw traces. Also adding a small note in model-onboard doc about kernel-fallback heuristic for long-contexts.
jena: Thanks all. overall — for new customers looking for low-p99 latency pick H100; for customers with long-tail budgeted reserved commit, run the reserved-price sensitivity and re-evaluate. :white_check_mark:
